topics.name: Autonomous driving perception and trajectory forecasting
topics.summary: These papers combine occlusion-aware planning, monocular range estimation, multimodal scene sensing, and route-conditioned trajectory prediction. Across road scenes and traffic infrastructure, they emphasize calibrated risk, long-horizon motion, and checks that reject unsafe or geometrically inconsistent behavior.

topics.name: Safe and robust robotic manipulation control
topics.summary: Learned disturbance models, reachability analysis, barrier functions, tactile transfer, and failure-aware retries support reliable contact-rich control. The applications span manipulators, assemblies, quadrotors, and other uncertain platforms where recovery and formal safety matter.

topics.name: Robot policy learning and visual reinforcement learning
topics.summary: These studies improve transfer by composing known skills, discovering reusable behaviors, and pretraining representations on video or self-supervised dynamics. The recurring goal is control that generalizes across tasks, bodies, appearances, and environments with fewer demonstrations.

topics.name: Robot motion planning, localization, and fleet coordination
topics.summary: Temporal-logic rewards, convex space-time planning, demonstration envelopes, learned localization, asynchronous state estimation, and reactive scheduling address constrained robot operation. The methods target reliable navigation and coordination despite disturbances, communication delays, and heterogeneous fleets.

topics.name: World models for embodied planning
topics.summary: Structured task state, terrain-aware simulation, predictive video rollouts, and fast learned evaluators help agents reason before acting over long horizons. These systems use predicted consequences to identify route failures, choose manipulation actions, and assess policies under changing scenes.

topics.name: Human-aware navigation and interactive robotics
topics.summary: Navigation systems combine persistent route memory, human queries, group-aware perception, and synchronized simulation to handle social context. User studies also examine how people perceive robot capability and how interactive experiments can be made repeatable.

topics.name: Multimodal model adaptation under distribution shift
topics.summary: Parameter isolation, modality-specific updates, smoothed objectives, and weight arithmetic provide inexpensive adaptation when deployment differs from training. The studies focus on retaining existing visual-language competence while transferring behavior from limited evidence or new sensory conditions.

topics.name: Multimodal reasoning and grounded visual learning
topics.summary: Latent-variable training, stochastic visual attention, structured instruction tuning, and step-level distillation make intermediate reasoning more useful and inspectable. The shared emphasis is preserving visual evidence while teaching models to connect observations, language, and generated explanations.

topics.name: Spatial reasoning and reliability in vision-language models
topics.summary: Counterfactual object changes, egocentric action choices, controlled depth stimuli, and scene-text interventions test whether models use geometry or rely on linguistic shortcuts. Results expose weaknesses in perspective, depth, attribution, and latency-sensitive visual decisions.

topics.name: Few-shot visual retrieval
topics.summary: Limited-label retrieval is improved through instance rejection, image-text composition, and compact cross-modal representations. These methods seek fine-grained matching while reducing false positives and overfitting when target categories or paired annotations are scarce.

topics.name: Structured visual representation learning
topics.summary: Hyperbolic geometry, language-derived concepts, coordinate supervision, reusable visual primitives, dense semantic objectives, and symmetry-aware interactions impose structure on learned features. The resulting representations support hierarchy, compositionality, transfer, and more interpretable visual recognition.

topics.name: Efficient visual perception and model compression
topics.summary: Adaptive tokenization, recursive computation, lightweight depth and segmentation models, pruning, and quantization reduce visual inference cost. The papers study variable deployment scales and task-specific quality loss across dense prediction, diffusion, and transformer architectures.

topics.name: Multi-view 3D reconstruction and geometry refinement
topics.summary: Sparse-view reconstruction, canonical correspondences, robust alignment, pose refinement, synthetic damage, and deformable aggregation address incomplete or unreliable imagery. Across animals, satellite scenes, and rendered objects, the methods improve global shape and cross-view consistency.

topics.name: Gaussian splatting and neural scene representations
topics.summary: Gaussian primitives provide a shared substrate for semantic grouping, volume compression, dynamic completion, texture enhancement, and novel-view rendering. Learned priors and weighted spatial aggregation improve storage, queryability, and consistency from sparse or monocular observations.

topics.name: Dynamic 3D scene understanding
topics.summary: Dense feature transfer, particle distributions, and discrete motion codes represent changing objects without depending on fragile continuous geometry. The recurring applications are semantic correspondence, instance association, and motion-aware scene interpretation over time.

topics.name: Controllable and efficient visual generation
topics.summary: Diffusion and flow-based generators are improved through fixed-point analysis, directional guidance, spatial conditioning, identity controls, and inference-time bias auditing. The studies balance fidelity, controllability, sampling stability, demographic fairness, and resource use in image and 3D generation.

topics.name: Text-to-audio and expressive avatar synthesis
topics.summary: Language-guided audio generation, flow-based synthesis, activation steering, blendshape or Gaussian deformation, and audio conditioning enable controllable speech, music, and expressive avatars. Common challenges include latency, speaker or identity preservation, emotional intensity, synchronization, and temporal stability.

topics.name: Audio perception and spoken interaction
topics.summary: Acoustic imaging, prototype-based open-set recognition, and probabilistic voice-activity modeling address unknown sounds and unnatural conversational timing. The methods emphasize covariance structure, rejection of unseen classes, and better turn-taking decisions from uncertain audio evidence.

topics.name: Long-context memory for language agents
topics.summary: Temporal graphs, replacement policies, artifact folding, recurrent caches, separated memory slots, and length-aware attention preserve useful information under tight context budgets. These systems reduce stale facts, overwrite errors, cache growth, and distractor dilution while testing durable recall.

topics.name: Neural retrieval and multimodal RAG
topics.summary: Latent query refinement, cluster-aware negatives, logical query decomposition, evidence packing, and retrieved image exemplars improve search and multimodal reasoning. The papers focus on selecting useful support under incomplete evidence, finite context, and competing documents.

topics.name: Evidence-grounded language-agent workflows
topics.summary: Failure taxonomies, span-level checks, uncertainty signals, runtime diagnoses, knowledge graphs, and structural appraisal make generated outputs easier to verify. Applications include analytical workflows, clinical extraction, document editing, credit reports, and code or tool execution.

topics.name: Reasoning post-training and preference alignment
topics.summary: Segment-level credit assignment, progressive multilingual supervision, interactive preferences, critic diagnostics, verifiable rewards, language critiques, procedural memory, and adaptive gradient weighting enrich post-training. Together they address reward sparsity, language transfer, alignment quality, stability, and diversity collapse.

topics.name: Efficient language-model inference and compression
topics.summary: Linear attention, hardware-specific runtimes, cache quantization, activation-guided updates, parallel decoding, and low-redundancy sampling reduce serving cost. The methods adjust memory or computation while preserving useful diversity and reserving more effort for difficult generations.

topics.name: Efficient language-model training and architecture
topics.summary: Data-mixture analysis, optimizer-state reduction, batch-size modeling, layer attribution, persistent-state pathways, and compact transformer components target cheaper training. The results favor structured allocation of data, memory, and computation over indiscriminate scaling.

topics.name: Mechanistic interpretability and knowledge debugging
topics.summary: Circuit interventions, model-organism comparisons, Fisher geometry, prototype neighborhoods, hallucination attribution, and interactive editing connect internal structure to observable behavior. These studies emphasize that conclusions depend on training setup, probing granularity, and the chosen measurement.

topics.name: AI robustness, adversarial security, and shortcut auditing
topics.summary: Stateful tool attacks, multimodal refusal failures, black-box architecture inference, memory and tool distribution shifts, causal interventions, and dataset shortcuts reveal weaknesses missed by standard accuracy tests. The papers motivate context-aware defenses and cross-domain evaluation.

topics.name: Generative media security and protection
topics.summary: Identity-document forensics, image-to-video protection, copyright safeguards, and refusal testing examine abuse at the boundary of generation and verification. The findings point to cross-domain weaknesses in current defenses and the need for stronger protection mechanisms.

topics.name: Evaluator and benchmark validity
topics.summary: Evaluator coupling, scaling metrics, physician and creativity judgments, judge calibration, audit protocols, and reproducibility checks show how measurement choices alter reported capability. Reliable comparisons require uncertainty, human alignment, fixed metadata, and sensitivity analysis.

topics.name: Multilingual and reasoning evaluation
topics.summary: Controlled tests of lexical restrictions, Japanese readings, cultural knowledge, cross-domain reasoning, and semi-supervised trace reuse separate language fluency from deeper capability. Results highlight knowledge dependence, rule-following failures, and negative transfer from poorly selected pseudo-solutions.

topics.name: Multimodal generation and hallucination evaluation
topics.summary: Diagnostic benchmarks examine unsupported motion, attribution errors, storyboard transitions, personalized subjects, and relationship preservation rather than relying on image similarity alone. Layered questions and human-aligned judgments expose perceptual and semantic failure modes.

topics.name: Persona calibration in conversational agents
topics.summary: Persona-conditioned answers vary with model family, scale, prompt format, and domain, while adaptive role selection links personality intensity to user goals and urgency. Together the studies argue against treating one fixed character as universally optimal.

topics.name: Agentic workflow assurance
topics.summary: Structured traces, online rule checks, deterministic tests, artifact validation, and expert-calibrated evaluation measure procedures as well as final answers. The applications span pathology, security artifacts, accessible web navigation, and service automation.

topics.name: Agent governance and coding-agent engineering
topics.summary: Software-agent studies connect permission boundaries, escalation design, dependency supply chains, runtime state, coding infrastructure, and enterprise adoption. Their recurring finding is that oversight and execution environments strongly shape reliability, cost, and practical productivity.

topics.name: Multi-agent communication and structured generation
topics.summary: Explicit message protocols, early branch termination, relational graphs, character goals, and persistent world records make distributed reasoning and open-ended generation more coherent. The studies link communication topology and intermediate structure to efficiency, traceability, and reuse.

topics.name: Scientific agents and autonomous experimentation
topics.summary: Simulation-grounded agricultural and chemical reasoning, editable literature search, statistically checked hypothesis exploration, and laboratory batch scheduling automate parts of the scientific loop. The common emphasis is tool-use accuracy, reproducibility, and auditable machine-led discovery.

topics.name: Interpretable machine learning and program synthesis
topics.summary: Concept graphs, feasible interventions, skill relationships, personalized rationales, example-based synthesis, and editable rule induction add human-readable structure to learned behavior. These approaches support diagnosis, decision support, and correction when supervision is incomplete or noisy.

topics.name: Medical image reconstruction and segmentation
topics.summary: Domain generalization, gated feature fusion, streaming MRI guidance, low-dose PET restoration, polarization recovery, k-space embeddings, registration confidence, and adaptive diagnosis improve clinical imaging under difficult acquisition conditions. The methods emphasize anatomy, boundaries, and reliability beyond raw pixel fidelity.

topics.name: Clinical ultrasound analysis
topics.summary: Prototype-based localization, anatomy-aware frame selection, and motion modeling support prenatal anomaly detection, fetal weight estimation, and cardiac phase recognition. These systems address operator variability and limited labels by exploiting temporal structure and reusable visual references.

topics.name: Clinical imaging benchmarks and diagnosis
topics.summary: Chest radiographs, lung CT, echocardiography, neural signals, cardiac measurements, MRI, and electronic records support disease recognition and risk prediction. The studies compare cohort shift, task-specific heads, anatomical supervision, frequency-aware features, and encoding choices.

topics.name: Interpretable biomedical prediction
topics.summary: Stable interaction-aware explanations for drug response and shared sparse predictors for mixed biological outcomes make correlated evidence easier to inspect. Both approaches preserve biological structure while seeking competitive prediction across multiple targets.

topics.name: Biomedical signal and affective computing
topics.summary: EEG adaptation, manifold alignment, self-supervised temporal features, and speech or text classifiers infer emotion, stress, cardiac state, and other physiological properties. The findings stress cross-subject variation, class imbalance, calibration, timing, and the limits of latent signal information.

topics.name: Molecular and atomistic machine learning
topics.summary: Molecular generation, reaction-rule induction, reinforcement learning, electrostatics-aware potentials, and equivariant spin representations connect chemical utility with physical structure. Applications include synthesis planning, ligand design, enzyme pathways, and efficient atomistic prediction.

topics.name: Scientific dynamical-systems modeling
topics.summary: Language-guided equation discovery, population parameter fitting, geometry-aware latent dynamics, probabilistic filtering, analytic region priors, and engineering graphs recover interpretable system behavior. The applications span PDE reduction, nonlinear processes, vibration, and high-dimensional state estimation.

topics.name: Time-series forecasting and representation
topics.summary: Physiological benchmarks, decision-aware point processes, ECG pretraining, streaming multivariate models, and regime-sensitive foundation-model evaluations study prediction under changing dynamics. The papers examine uncertainty, transfer, continual updates, attribution, and how protocol choices affect reported accuracy.

topics.name: Remote sensing and ecological monitoring
topics.summary: Satellite time series, land-cover maps, artificial-light measurements, and canopy-height estimation connect geospatial modeling with biodiversity and environmental monitoring. The studies account for spatial scale, sampling effort, and uncertain labels when mapping ecological change.

topics.name: Generative and industrial anomaly detection
topics.summary: Diffusion reconstruction, active temporal sampling, risk-preference distillation, feedback loops, and minimax objectives improve detection without abundant anomaly labels. Applications include counterfeit printing and contaminated industrial time series, with emphasis on subtle deviations and efficient evidence gathering.

topics.name: Optimization under limited feedback
topics.summary: Differentiable cardinality control, distributed submodular learning, generative-prior black-box search, novelty pressure, and resource redistribution address expensive or delayed evaluation. The studies measure regret, portfolio quality, exploration diversity, and recovery in changing or deceptive landscapes.

topics.name: Quantum machine learning
topics.summary: Quantum kernels, variational models, neural quantum states, ensemble methods, and hybrid-data benchmarks examine possible benefits under hardware and sample constraints. Results compare quantum and classical baselines while probing optimization, noise filtering, causal physical features, and false-positive control.

topics.name: Federated learning
topics.summary: Synthetic-data methods, automated recipe search, class-aware momentum, adaptive sampling, privacy noise, and Byzantine analysis address skewed data and unreliable clients. The papers combine practical evaluation with theory on convergence, robustness, and how privacy can alter generalization.

topics.name: Human-centered AI and accessible visualization
topics.summary: Gaze-aware narration, mixed-reality interaction, robot capability perception, developer delegation, tactile charts, and animated visual explanations study how people interpret and use AI systems. The applications emphasize accessibility, belief correction, interaction cost, and human judgment.

topics.name: Personalized intent modeling
topics.summary: Facet-aware peer signals and behavior-conditioned search infer intent from individual history rather than broad population demand. The results show that personalized context can resolve ambiguous queries and improve recommendations or product search.

topics.name: Document layout and structure recognition
topics.summary: Semantic zones, OCR-aware reading-order modeling, language guidance, asymmetric edge supervision, and table boundary detection improve document parsing. The methods target noisy newspapers and real-time tables where geometric structure matters as much as text recognition.

topics.name: Visual tracking and wildlife monitoring
topics.summary: Fine-grained spatial-temporal experts, adaptive tracking, and detector tuning stabilize identity and reduce false alarms as targets deform or backgrounds change. Applications cover person re-identification, generic object tracking, and camera-trap conservation footage.

topics.name: Long-video understanding and temporal grounding
topics.summary: Audio-visual alignment benchmarks, query-difficulty routing, keyframe selection, entity-event memory, and recurrent latent caches preserve evidence over extended videos. The systems improve localization and grounded answering when relevant events are sparse or processed incrementally.

topics.name: Video super-resolution
topics.summary: Geometry-aware light-field processing, recurrent diffusion features, and scale-conditioned decoding restore detail across arbitrary magnification factors. The recurring constraints are ray consistency, temporal coherence, and preservation of structure rather than isolated frame sharpness.

topics.name: Agent-based urban mobility simulation
topics.summary: Synthetic populations, semantic trajectories, route-choice models, social behavior, and network-scale pedestrian flows create configurable environments for testing mobility interventions. The methods connect high-level goals with physical movement and measurable crowd responses.

topics.name: Annotation-efficient and synthetic-data learning
topics.summary: Active selection combines uncertainty, coverage, stage dependencies, and temporal feasibility, while dataset condensation and digital-twin feedback generate useful training examples. The shared objective is preserving transfer and detection quality with fewer expert labels or target observations.

topics.name: Transportation infrastructure vision
topics.summary: Visual pipelines convert railway-crossing imagery and aerial observations into risk estimates and topology-aware lane maps. Their domain-specific outputs emphasize geometry, safety decisions, and expert agreement beyond generic image classification.

topics.name: Immersive interaction sensing
topics.summary: In-air movement signatures support identity verification in virtual reality, while bounded look-ahead during training improves causal gaze prediction without requiring future frames at deployment. Both study temporal and spatial cues for embodied interfaces.
